paper.title: Volumetric Spanners: an Efficient Exploration Basis for Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit Linear Optimization (BLO) over general convex sets
unmapped: Loss vectors chosen from the polar of K: |L_t^T x| <= 1 for all x in K
settings.definition_quote: iteratively at each time sequence $t$, the environment chooses a loss vector $L_t$ that is not revealed to the player. The player chooses a vector $x_t \in \K$ where $\K \subseteq \reals^d$ is convex, and once she commits to her choice, the loss $\ell_t = x_t^\top L_t$ is revealed. ... The set $\K$ is equipped with a membership oracle. ... The losses are bounded in absolute values by 1 ... (by an oblivious adversary)

symbols.s_sp: maximum size of the exploration set S_t over rounds, max_t |S_t|

source.label: thm:geo hedge
source.quote: Under the assumptions stated above, and let $s=\max_t |S_t|$, $ \eta = \sqrt{\frac{\log |\K|_{1/T}}{dT}}$ and let $\gamma = s\sqrt{\frac{\log(|\K|_{1/T})}{dT}} $. Algorithm \ref{alg:BLO} given parameters $\gamma,\eta$ suffers a regret bounded by $$ O\left(  (s+d)\sqrt{\frac{T \log |\K|_{1/T} }{d}} \right)$$

results.notes: Proof bounds expected regret. Theorem numbering inferred (section 6).

source.quote: There exist an efficient algorithm for BLO for any convex set $\K$ with regret of $$ O\left(  \sqrt{dT \log |\K|_{1/T}  } \right) = O\left(  d\sqrt{T \log(T)  } \right) $$

results.notes: Uses s=d via barycentric-spanner-based ratio spanner; polynomial runtime via approximate log-concave sampling.
